text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Swedish papers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Companies are the largest tax evaders in Sweden with 3,000 companies owing the government more than 15 billion crowns.
- United Nations (UN) Secretary-General Kofi Annan will ask Swedish Defence Minister Bjorn von Sydow for a Swedish UN force on Tuesday during Annan's visit to Sweden.
- Investment company Custos will become a new large owner of transport company ASG by bidding for Transportforvaltning, which holds 27.1 percent of votes and 16.5 percent of capital in ASG.

- Analysts should cut their forecasts for truckmaker Scania, a commentator writes. The price war in the truck market in Sweden is not a temporary phenonmenon and Scania will have an especially hard time competing because of its size.
- Sweden's highway authority writes in a report that it would like to prevent young people from driving motorcycles and mopeds because the number of accidents they have is so high.

- The Swedish job market is improving, figures from the National Labour Board (Ams) show. Ams outgoing general director Gote Bernhardsson says optimism from the spring will continue into the autumn. The figure showed unemployment rose to 10.8 percent in July from 9.4 percent in June, although it said the number of lay-offs fell.

- Sweden's state debt is falling for the first time in seven years. In July it fell by 0.6 billion crowns after increasing every month in the 1990s. In 1998 the surplus could be 10 billion crowns and the National Debt Office recommends the money is used to repay part of the debt.
- Investment company Incentive posted a higher than expected result for the first six months of the year with sales of 10.3 billion crowns and profit after financial items of 11.7 billion.
- Market rumours say a competing bid is expected for real estate group Gotic. State-owned Vasakronan has already placed a bid on the group.
